dossier.public_summary: Light curve shows a strong wobble at the same period as the dip, with huge spot variations and a duration that does not match a planet on the star. This is the signature of a spotted star, not a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Star varies by 6615 ppm at this period, ratio_to_depth 0.7261 with chi2 1037 dof 7 - much larger out-of-transit swing than dip, favours spots/variability or close binary over planet

Tool rotation finds stellar spot period 0.8374999999999999 d equals signal 0.837023 d (signal_over_rotation 0.999430447761194), sector amplitudes 68616 ppm, 55396 ppm, 31237 ppm, 33172 ppm, 36863 ppm, 47046 ppm with false_alarm 0.0 - dip at exact rotation period is classic spot signal

Transit duration 1.632x central_h (observed 2.48 h vs central 1.52 h) and stellar_density_penalty 15660 show star's density is wrong for a planetary transit, inconsistent with a planet on this K dwarf

Depth changes 94.28% from 12902 ppm (sector 16) to 5362 ppm (sector 23) vs 7389-7871 ppm elsewhere; sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with p_constant_all 1.964091241429466e-24 - true astrophysical depth change, not calibration
ML scorer ranks as very planet-unlike (median planet 0.5, below 0.1 only 1 in 10 planets score this low), consistent with stellar false positive
